figures.caption: Fig. 2. The setup and the design grid. A sample is a stream of 25 bits, the first 10 washout; the target is the majority or the parity of the last w bits, shifted back by d. The figure lists the levels of each design factor (Table 2 in the appendix) and the windows and delays of the task variants; only the linear readout is trained.

Fig. 3. Design accuracy of the best design at each input fan-out and injection (w=5), final-state readout (left) and summed (right). The best design over k̄, ticks, initialization and self-loops is chosen per task variant on the selection run (Sect. 3.4). Colour: task; line style: delay (solid d=5, dotted d=10); marker: injection (filled override, open xor). Dashed grey line: the floor of summed majority (70.7 % at both delays).

Fig. 4. The optimal connectivity k̄∗ against input fan-out (categorical axis), final-state readout (left) and summed (right). Solid lines: k̄∗ of each task, from the mean designaccuracy curve over all designs at that fan-out and k̄ and over the task’s four variants (windows and delays); bars span the k̄ within 1 % of the accuracy at k̄∗. Dashed lines: the k̄ at the peak of the mean ∆ curve over the same designs; ∆ does not depend on the task, so each readout has one. Fan-out 1 is left out: its mean curves are within 1 % of their peak from k̄=3.5–5 up to 8. At fan-out 4 the parity bars run to k̄=8, beyond the axis.
Table 2. The design factors of the grid (Fig. 2), their values, and what each controls. Every factor is defined in Sect. 3.1.

Fig. 5. Replication of Snyder et al.’s kernel-quality curve: the rank of the final reservoir states over 25 streams drawn from all 210 ten-bit streams, against k̄ (|R|=25). Shared pool: the wiring of Snyder et al., where input and recurrent edges come from one pool. Separate draw: the input edges drawn on their own, as many on average as in the shared pool. Dedicated: the one-to-one mapping at input fan-out r=1, 3 and 5. Under the shared pool and the separate draw, few or no nodes receive the input at low k̄; the dedicated mapping at r=5 raises KQ there. Lines: smoothing splines through the means over 25 reservoirs at each k̄; the numbers in the text are the means at the grid points.

Table 3. Average marginal effect of each factor at the operating point, in %, from a Beta regression per readout and task (logit link; baseline one tick, random initialization, no self-loops; standard errors clustered by design). Ticks and initialization: at the operating point’s k̄, with self-loops as a control. Self-loops: each combination at its own k̄∗, with ticks and initialization as controls. Brackets: 95 % interval from 2,000 coefficient draws.

Fig. 7. ∆ against design accuracy at the operating point, final-state majority at w=5, one point per design; colour gives the fraction s of nodes with a self-loop, filled markers one tick and open markers two. (a) Delay 5: ∆ and accuracy fall together as s rises, and within each s the one-tick designs are the more accurate; within an s level ρ = 0.74, the mean over the levels. (b) Delay 10: below s=1 the second tick raises the mean ∆ of a level and lowers its accuracy, so within an s level ∆ ranks the designs in reverse (ρ = −0.38, the mean over the levels).
